Feb 16, 2026

Bob

Color: Blue

Sold by RR Healthy Delivered by Walmart

5 out of 5 stars review

### This blue knee walker is fantastic. Buy it.

Got the knee walker three days after breaking my left leg. Assembly was easy, but the directions were worthless. A 10 year old could get better pictures on how to assemble the walker. Fortunately there are videos online. I am very mechanical after working on copy machines for 29 years. I just unpacked it on the dining room table (covered) and only had one screw in the wrong place, easily switched. I weigh 230 lbs and fly down the hardwood hallway. Visiting nurses are always impressed. It will go on my graveled driveway with difficulty and I need help getting it into a car. Easy to go backwards and to pick up the front while the back is down to turn around. Been using it for 2 week now and no complaints. Would buy again, and will store for another problem in my 80 years of life. Wish I'd had it with my crushed leg in 2010, or cut foot in 2019.

Easy to put together. Comes mostly assembled. Instruction booklet not perfect but knee scooter and parts clearly marked and visible. Thought I was missing a part but I wasn't. Customer servive quickly stepped up to offer help. Shipped out and delivered very fast. Quality mobility scooter. I highly reccomend it.

I would recommend this idem to anyone who's having leg issues or maybe 🤔 some kind of foot surgeries and needs to stay off their feet and also its used be recommended to older people who have a hard time getting around period. But honestly it's really good for just about every day use for anyone who's in need of help. Thank You and have a wonderful day.

May 11, 2025

Valerie

### A real life saver in my time of need

I purchased this knee scooter due to right foot surgery where I have been unable to walk or drive for over a month now. If it wasn't for this little scooter I don't know what I would've done as I had no one to help me and just couldn't manage the crutches. This scooter enabled me to get around my home and eventually out in my yard and even on the street. My home is small and it doesn't turn on a dime but it sure beats crutches. At first I thought it was too unstable for anything but flat level surfaces but discovered by adjusting seat and handle bars to the lowest possible positions comfortable to me that soon I was able to maneuver it anywhere in my yard and even on the street w/o worry it might fall over. It is a real lifesaver in my time of need, I don't know how I would manage to get by until I can walk again w/o it. I wanted to give it 4 1/2 stars but you can't tap a half star in.🙂⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️1/2

Jan 5, 2026

Heather

### Uncomfortable and just basic

The directions were not very detailed, which made assembly a bit hard. This made me uncomfortable because I didn't want this put together incorrectly and cause further injury or a new injury if it wasn't safely assembled. Once it was put together, I tried it around the home and it's extremely fast and has no resistance at all. It almost feels too loose for the purpose, since this should be taken slow. I can use the brakes, but overall, it's not the most comfortable and doesn't make me feel confident when using.

### Ok in a pinch.

This is not for short people! i am 5'5", and it didn't adjust low enough. I bought platforms to compensate. I also had an issue with the seat kinda breaking down, but I think that might have been the way I was using it.

Sep 11, 2025

### Ask for price adjustment

The same scooter you charge me 89.99 and it's showing 79.99 today same brand was not please with the different price same brand but it's nice.

Dec 22, 2025

### Unstable and unsafe

Although it was an easy assembly parts were missing along with caps to cover the screws. Because of this the item is wobbly and my pants leg/shoe gets caught on the exposed screw. I have fallen multiple times maneuvering around. The cushion is not secured and uncomfortable. I have ordered another scooter from a different company and this sits in a corner

Jul 28, 2025

### Poor product and customer service

Ordered this for surgery. Arrived on time, however it was obvously used. Had scratches and parts missing. Whoever had it before tried to put it together and had assembled it incorrectly--perhaps that is why it was not foldable. Contacted Walmart and they told me to keep it and they would contact me about the refund. Then days later I was told to return it.

Jul 5, 2025

### Not so safe!

People, think very carefully before you purchase! The reason I bought the knee scooter was because I have a broken leg. So, the very first time I tried to use it the steering was too tight, making it difficult to scoot. When I applied the brakes one didn't work and the wheel came around and hit me in the ankle, taking the skin off! Now I have one broken leg and the other ankle is bruised and swollen.

 Susanna (Providence, US) 

Well-made, sturdy knee walker -liked it so much, bought another for my second floor!

Bought this knee walker for use after an extensive foot and ankle surgery and found it much more affordable than renting as I'll need it for several months. I was fortunate to be able to see one in person at a local medical supply, so I knew I was getting a quality scooter, but it's even better than I expected! It arrived very quickly and was easy to assemble and get started. It's very sturdy but still quite maneuverable and not overly heavy. The cutout knee pad is wonderfully supportive while relieving pressure on the shin, and it is quite comfortable. I purchased a separate cushion but found it unnecessary and less safe as it didn't stay in place well. I needed help from customer service for my initial order, and received competent, caring assistance. My only complaint is that the backpack attachment is too low on the knee walker, and I find it unstructured and a nuisance to have to open and close. I purchased the basket separately and it was a nice upgrade -higher and easier to reach, easy to get items in and out with one hand (so I can hold the handlebar with the other), and nice pockets. I feel that for the price of the knee walker, it would be great to have the choice of backpack or basket when purchasing rather than requiring a separate purchase. Overall, this knee scooter is a very good value and worth the money spent.

 A 

 Andrea Schuster (Cadillac, US) 

Easy Assembly & Very Sturdy. Exactly What We Needed!

I ordered this scooter/walker for my husband after he ruptured his Achilles Tendon and had surgery to repair it. He's going to be laid up for awhile and I figured this would be a bit more comfortable than having to use crutches all the time. I also ordered additional accessories to go with it, phone holder, knee walker pad...all great investments. The scooter went together so easy, and has been very easy to take with us when we need to go somewhere. Hubby loves being able to use the scooter vs the crutches whenever possible and says it is very easy to maneuver and is very comfortable. The brakes work very well also...don't ask how we know! LOL!

Hi Andrea! Thank you for sharing your positive experience with the Knee Walker for your husband! ## FAQ

#### What is the weight capacity?

300 lbs.

#### Does the knee walker come with a bag?

Yes, the removable bag comes free with your purchase.

#### Why is the knee scooter causing my knee pain?

When using for extended periods try our knee pad cover for add extra padding and comfort.

#### Is this an all terrain knee walker?

Yes, the 8 inch wheels provide a smooth ride on indoor and outdoor surfaces.

#### Do you offer any knee walker accessories?

Yes, every walker comes with a carry bag. Consider our pad cover if you need extra padding.

#### How comfortable is the knee pad?

The foam knee cushion is ergonomically designed to contour to the leg. It allows weight to be evenly distributed across the knee platform and supplies better air circulation for a comfortable user experience.

#### How heavy is the knee scooter?

25 lbs.

#### How do I get replacement parts?

Call us at 1-800-487-3808 or by email. We would be happy to provide you any parts you need.

## Specifications

Product Details:

- Knee Pad Height: Adjustable between 18"-23"
- Handle Bar Height: Adjustable in 1" increments ranging from 33" to 41"
- Knee Pad Dimensions: 14" x 7" (at widest part)
- Front Wheels + Frame: 16" across (widest point of scooter)
- Four 8-inch polyurethane wheels provide an exceptionally stable base for easy maneuverability both indoors and outdoors.
- Two fold points and the removable platform allows the scooter to be easily transported.
- Weight limit 300 LBS

Assembly:

Minimal assembly required

All tools required for assembly included

For more detail reference our manual

Operating Instructions:

Center injured leg on the knee pad, covering the entire length of the padding

Standing as straight as possible, propel yourself forward using uninjured leg

Engage the security lock before attempting to transfer from the knee walker

Braking:

- Walker is equipped with a dual wheel braking system.
- To adjust the brakes, turn cable adjuster located on the hand brake.

Adjusting Pad Height:

Loosen locking lever under the knee pad

Remove locking pin

Adjust knee pad to desired height and replace locking pin to secure it in place

Adjusting Handle Height:

- Loosen adjustment screw on the handle by turning it counterclockwise until it can be removed
- Adjust handle bar grip to the desired height

*The knee walker is designed with both height adjustable knee pad and handle height to accommodate users 5'1" to 6'6"

Product is designed for people recovering from:

- Foot surgery
- Broken leg, ankle or foot
- Sprained leg, ankle or foot
- Ulcers of the foot

What's Included:

- Knee walker
- Storage bag

Guarantee Policy:

- frame - 1 year
- brakes / handles - 90 days
- wheels - none / on arrival 30 days
- screws / bolts / nuts - none / on arrival 30 days
- cushions / seats - none / on arrival 30 days
- paint / panels - none / on arrival 30 days

Product Number: MOB1007BLK (Black); MOB1007PNK (Pink)

Shipping Weight: 25.5 pounds

# ELENKER Steerable Knee Walker with 10" Front Wheels Deluxe Medical Scooter for Foot Injuries Compact Crutches Alternative Black
Brand: ELENKER
Category: Mobility Aids & Equipment > Walkers, Rollators & Accessories

## Features
Travel-friendly Design The Knee Walker is designed for indoor and outdoor use, allowing users to move anywhere. You no longer need to worry about not being able to move. Perfect for getting around your home, work, supermarket or park. Please note For your safety, do not slide at high speed. Recommended speed 1m/s.; Textured 10" Front wheels With durable and non-slip PVC wheels and a wider front axle increases stability,the knee scooter provides greater stability for those with poor balance.; Speed Up Your Recovery Ideal for individuals recovering from an injury or surgery to the foot, ankle or lower leg, as well as for individuals with below-the-knee amputations.; Safe and Durable With its easy-grip handlebars and dual braking system, the walker is designed to keep you safe. The dual locking system on both brakes offer extra safety when you intend to hold the walker firmly still.; Convenient Using crutches requires great upper body strength, rubs under the armpits ,and is unstable. This knee walker is made for both indoor and outdoor use, it is a hands free / pain free crutch alternative and offers the most versatility among knee walkers.; FSA HSA approved products, eligible for reimbursement.

# Drive Medical Adult Knee Walker Crutch Alternative
Brand: Drive Medical
Category: Walkers, Rollators & Accessories > Rolling Walkers

## Features
Ideal for individuals recovering from foot surgery, breaks, sprains, amputation, and ulcers of the foot; Deluxe lever brake ensures safety ; Leg pad with "Channel" provides added stability and comfort; Can be adjusted for either right, or left-handed use; Tool-free leg and handle-height adjustment; Overall Dimensions: 32"(L) x 14"(W) x 32.5"(H); Knee Pad Dimensions: 14.25"(L) x 7.5"(W) x 18"-22"(H); Handle Height: 32.5"-41"; Weight Capacity: 300 lbs

## Pricing & Reviews
Rated 3.8 from 366 reviews.
Top review: The best word to describe the Drive Knee Walker is "Freedom." If you are stuck with crutches, then you know what I mean. With the Drive knee walker, you have one hand free to carry stuff, like a glass of milk or a sandwich. I even took my two dogs for a short walk (maybe not the brightest thing I could do, but I did it-try walking a greyhound using crutches).This model does not have a steering mechanism, but I did not find that to be a problem. You simply lift the front of the device and point it where you want to go. A handbrake on the rear wheels is invaluable to stop and use to position the knee walker when changing directions in tight spaces.The wheels are larger than most similar knee walkers. I used the Drive knee walker to attend a football game in the Horseshoe and photograph a wedding in the woods. I could not have done either with crutches.The knee walker arrived several days sooner than promised and it is well built. These folks exceeded all my expectations!The wheels and handle are easily adjusted. I am 6'2" and set the wheels in the middle adjustment. I would not recommend this to someone under 5'6". but this is just a guess. It comes in five pieces and you have to attach each of the four wheels, but that is not difficult. 10-20 minutes max.The frame folds with the front and back wheels meeting. Once folded, it is probably 16" wide or so. I sat in the front seat of the car with the device between my legs. It weighs just under 18 pounds so it is not too heavy, but it might be for a lady. I even locked the brake and sat on the short platform several times, although I would not recommend this for a long sit.You will find that you use different muscles than with crutches. Don't go crazy, like I did, the first week or two of use. If you lift it a lot you will feel soreness in your chest. I never felt that I might fall with the knee walker as I did with crutches. It just feels so much safer to use than crutches.The only drawback is that my knee, while it felt no pain, developed a spot of skin that dried out, cracked and bled. I wore mostly shorts while using the Drive knee walker so my bare skin was in contact with the padded platform. The platform could use a bit more padding and if I need to use the knee walker again for any length of time, I plan to add some padding.My only regret was that I learned of the Drive knee walker a month after my foot surgery. I ordered it right away. It significantly improve my quality of life while recovering. I suppose any similar device would do the same.I have a friend who had knee surgery and used a knee walker with a steering wheel. He said it was too bulky and did not use it long. I saw a gentleman at a restaurant with one like that and the wheels were dinky compared to the Drive model.The price I paid was significantly less than any other similar knee walker.Personally, for my needs, I would recommend the Drive model I bought over one with steering.

The legs and handles can be height adjusted to accommodate most users.

Top review: I've read a few criticisms of this knee stroller, but I don't have any complaints at all so far. I've used it only 5 days, so these are first impressions. The brake is a bit hard to lock. I'm a 6', 200lb man who is in pretty good condition and I have to squeeze the brake handles pretty hard to engage the lock. But I've gotten to where I can do it with one hand. The brakes are pretty secure when engaged. I read one reviewer who said their brakes rubbed on the wheels when not engaged, but that's not the case for me. I haven't made any adjustments and the breaks fully disengage and the wheels roll freely.I expect my house is pretty typical in not have lots of large open spaces - not like in ELenker's videos! Maneuvering is a bit of a challenge in tight spaces. I do lots of laps around the kitchen island so that I don't have to backup or do multi-point turns. But I haven't found any issues with stability. I try to keep both hands on the handlebar, but have done a few short, slow rolls with only one hand.Most of the flooring in my house is 18" porcelain tiles. The knee stroller rolls really well on tiles. But if you get the wheels lined up in a grout line, it does tend to grab the wheel. That makes turning a bit tricky as you will feel the wheels grab in the grout lines. Rolling on the carpeted areas works OK but definitely not as smooth as on the tiles.So far, the knee pad is comfortable. I did not buy an accessory pad. I'm just using the bare knee pad as it came from Elenker.One bit of irony is that they ship the knee stroller to you with assembly required. Here I am with a broken ankle having to unbox and assemble this thing. Assembly would be super easy if I didn't have a broken ankle. With a broken ankle, it was a bit more challenging. The one thing about the assembly instructions is that details about the bolts is missing. They send bolts of 3 different lengths, but with no indication which bolt to use in each location. I ended up using the shortest bolt on the seat post, the two medium bolts on the steering column and the long bolt on the body connection.I expect to be using this thing for at least 2 more months and I'll try to let you know how it holds up.
